info.name: CallCenter - Multi-Client IVR Platform
info.description:
Follows the platform's real story end to end: onboard two independent clients (Apex Bank, Swift Loan Recovery) -> each designs their own flow (typed prompts + optional real audio + a data lookup) -> create a campaign atomically linked to that flow -> watch it pre-synthesize every prompt BEFORE the worker is allowed to dial anyone ('preparing' -> 'running') -> prove neither client can see or touch the other's flow or campaign. Run folders top to bottom - each request's Tests script saves IDs/tokens into collection variables that later requests consume automatically.

Note: the Dinstar SIM gateway may be offline - if so, campaigns still create/prepare/link correctly, they just won't physically ring a phone until the gateway is back online. Everything through the dial attempt can be verified without it.

request.description: No auth required. Confirms the backend is up and shows live postgres/redis/AMI connection status.
This is the ONE account that can onboard new clients (POST /api/auth/clients is super_admin-gated). Every client's own admin, created in folder 1, only ever manages their own tenant from here on.

Creates a brand-new tenant + its first client_admin login + grants them SIM ports 0 and 1, all in ONE atomic request - portNumbers is mandatory, not an optional follow-up step. This is the entire onboarding step for a new business - no code changes, ever, per client. If you've already run this collection before, you'll get a 409 (tenant/username already exists) - that's fine, just continue to 1.3.

request.description: From here on, {{bank_admin_token}} is used for every Apex Bank request below - it carries their tenant_id in the JWT, which is what every /api/ivr/* and /api/campaigns/* endpoint filters by.

Sets Apex Bank's allocation to EXACTLY this list - adding port 2 on top of the 0,1 they got at onboarding. "Increase" and "decrease" are the same endpoint, just a longer or shorter portNumbers array. If port 2 is already held by a different tenant from earlier testing, you'll correctly get a 400 - pick a genuinely free port number instead.

Same endpoint, shorter list - releases ports 1 and 2 back to the free pool (their tenant_id goes back to null) and leaves Apex Bank with just port 0. Check folder 3's campaign requests afterward to see allowedPorts now defaults to just "0".

item.name: 2. Apex Bank Designs Its Own Flow
2.1 Upload a Real Recorded Prompt (optional path)

request.description: Path 1 of 2 for getting a prompt onto the box: upload a real recording, get back a prompt_id to reference in a node. Transcodes + delivers to the Asterisk box automatically. The flow below uses this for its welcome node, and typed text (path 2) for everything else, to show both working side by side.

Sample CSV (provider_number/provider_name columns) - swap this file for your own client data (account numbers, loan IDs, policy numbers, whatever your lookup node needs to key on) and adjust keyColumn to match your header. This is the 'table' source option for a lookup node; a client with their own backend can point at a webhook instead.

item.name: 2.3 Create Flow (typed prompts + uploaded audio + lookup, all in one)

request.description: One flow, demonstrating everything: welcome uses an uploaded recording (prompt_id); menu/collect_account/not_found_node are just TYPED text (prompt_text) - no audio file needed, Piper speaks them; speak_result's prompt_text contains {{'{{'}}provider_name{{'}}'}}, a value that only exists once the lookup runs mid-call - that's a flow VARIABLE, not a Postman variable, leave it exactly as-is. Real DTMF branching (1 -> lookup, 9 -> hangup), a data lookup, and dynamic TTS readback, all client-authored as plain JSON. This is a sample scenario - design your actual flow the same way, with your own content.
Reads the flow back - confirms all 7 nodes persisted, with client_id references resolved to real database UUIDs, and prompt_text stored alongside prompt_id per node.

item.name: 3.1 Create Campaign (atomically linked to the flow)

request.description:
REPLACE {{test_phone_number}} with your own real number if you want this to actually ring you. {{test_language_code}} defaults to en-US - change to hi-IN or mr-IN to test another installed voice, per-lead, with zero flow changes.

ivrFlowId links the campaign to the flow in the SAME insert as creation (no separate activate-after-create race). No audio file is required - the flow supplies its own prompts.

Response status will be "preparing" (not "running") since this flow has static prompt_text - the backend pre-synthesizes every prompt for every language your leads use BEFORE the worker is allowed to dial anyone. This is what closes the ~20-second dead-air bug that used to happen live on the first call to a never-before-spoken phrase. Move on to 3.2 and poll until it flips.

Click Send repeatedly (every few seconds) until campaign.status reads "running" instead of "preparing" - that's your signal every prompt for this campaign's language(s) is already sitting on the Asterisk box, so the very first call plays audio instantly instead of going silent for ~20s. While status is "preparing", the worker will NOT touch this campaign's leads at all (dial_status stays "pending", attempts stays 0) - check the leads array below to see that for yourself.

Also confirms campaign.ivr_flow_id equals bank_flow_id from step 2.3 - proof the whole chain wired together.

request.description: A SECOND dedicated tenant, on a different port (1) - exists purely so 5.5 and 5.12 below have a real, deterministic "someone else's port" to attempt to steal, without reaching into Apex Bank's or Swift Loans' port allocations from folder 1.

item.name: 5.5 Onboard Conflict: Request a Port Port Test Co Already Owns -> 400, Full Rollback

request.description:
Port 7 belongs to Port Test Co (granted in 5.2, deterministically, within this same folder) - onboarding must ROLL BACK ENTIRELY on a port conflict, not just skip the port grant, otherwise you'd end up with a half-onboarded tenant+admin that has zero ports and no way to tell it apart from a deliberately-unrestricted one. Run 5.6 right after this to prove the admin login was never actually created.

If you've run this folder before and Conflict Co already exists from a prior pass, you'll get a 409 here instead of 400 - that's a leftover from an earlier run, not a bug; the 400+rollback behavior was already proven that time.

exec: pm.test('Blocked - port already allocated to another tenant (or already ran before)', function () {

item.name: 5.6 Confirm Rollback: Conflict Co Admin Cannot Log In -> 401

request.description:
Proves 5.5's ROLLBACK actually undid the whole transaction (tenant + admin user), not just the port grant - if this login ever succeeds, onboarding is silently leaving orphaned half-configured clients behind on a port conflict.

Note: if 5.5 returned 409 (Conflict Co already existed from an earlier run), this login will correctly succeed (200) instead - that's expected in that case, not a rollback failure.

exec: pm.test('No admin account exists - rollback was complete (unless 5.5 hit a pre-existing 409)', function () {

request.description: This route used to be entirely zero-auth (anyone could see the full port-to-tenant mapping, including other clients' tenant names). Confirms that gap is closed - no token, no data.
